Krakovets New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · L'vivs'ka oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Jewish life in Krakovets traces back to the mid-17th century, growing to a peak of just over 1,000 residents — 53 percent of the town — by 1880, when the community supported three synagogues and two cemeteries. Numbers fell steadily through the early 20th century to about 340 by 1931; after occupation in the summer of 1941, dozens of Jews were killed in 1942, the remaining community was expelled to the Yavoriv ghetto that December, and more than 20 people found in hiding were murdered in January 1943. This cemetery was demolished in the 1960s, and today the land is used by locals for cattle grazing.
